text.p: UK property company Greycoat Plc said on Thursday that shareholders had voted to reject a resolution calling for the sale of all its assets.
The group said in a statement that 95 percent of those shareholders who voted had rejected the proposal, which was put forward by shareholder the UK Active Value Fund (UKAV).
UKAV, representing 10.6 percent of the issued share capital, did not vote on its resolution.
"This result shows an overwhelming majority against UKAV's proposal and 95 percent support for our management and its strategy," Greycoat's chairman Michael Beckett said.
"We can now get back to work without this costly distraction," Beckett said.

Earlier, shareholders had voted unanimously on a show of hands to reject the UKAV proposal at a reconvened extraordinary general meeting. Beckett called the poll so that the views of shareholders not able to attend the meeting could vote.
Of the issued share capital, 54.8 percent voted against the resolution with only 2.9 percent voting in favour.
Shares in Greycoat, which is also the subject of a merger proposal by its smaller rival Moorfield Estates, were unchanged at 163.5 pence at 1420 GMT.

Beckett told shareholders at the special meeting that the UKAV had done "nothing to add value for shareholders" and said the board saw its activities "as having been positively damaging to shareholders interests".
